contractsVerified: Run and bridge processes share one cross-process registry, unique ID namespace and bounded quota
Windows OS process start time and executable identity gate stop, cancel and orphan reclaim; PID reuse fails closed
A real detached Godot process is reclaimed after its owner is killed, and a dead-owner registry lock is recovered
Repeated or globally reserved session IDs cannot overwrite earlier live records; double stop is idempotent
Mutating bridge calls carry operation IDs; cancelled writes report UNKNOWN and late results can be queried without replay
HTTP DELETE and idle lease, stdio EOF/signals, and scenario cleanup have independent bounded stop paths
Real HTTP and stdio client tests stop both owned launch and bridge processes and record terminal states
limitations: Operation status is process-local and cannot establish whether a crashed in-flight write committed; clients must re-read state
Linux verified PID signalling is unavailable and remains UNSUPPORTED for live orphan termination
HTTP idle cleanup is bounded by the configured lease (default five minutes), not immediate after a silent disconnect
A reused owner PID or abandoned recovery guard can leave the registry fail-closed until intervention
G1 is NOT_RUN until T08 is complete; this evidence does not confer production qualification
Raw runs are Git-ignored and must be rerun if unavailable after migration
